text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Gerakan party has sacked parlimentarian and tycoon Joseph Chong as a member of its central committee for causing dissension within the party. Chong's supporters had on Thursday submitted his nomination to bid for the post of party president in Oct 5 internal elections.

-- Malaysian women married to foreign workers will be allowed to stay here or follow their husbands home, said Home Ministry secretary-general Samsudin Osman. Malaysia on Thursday said short-term foreign workers who marry local women will be immediately deported.

-- Central bank, Bank Negara will call all commercial banks and financial services companies soon to discuss ways to re-employ its personnels who opt to leave, said Deputy Governor Fong Weng Phak. Bank Negara on Monday announced it was slashing about 700 jobs, a quarter of its present staff.
